diagnosis: A rule propagating through kernel_propagate directly forced literal 10 at level 0. Only propagate_service and the probing/binary propagators published newly forced root literals, so 10 stayed implicit in the native-DSR proof. SubstitutionRedundancy then wrote the witnessed unit '1 1' while (-1 v 10) was live. The step is valid, and forward dsr-trim emits the RAT hint group, but a backward checker knows 10 only as an implied unit, cannot cite it for the satisfied candidate, and emits '33 1 1 0 0' with no group; Trestle rejects that LSR. Writing '10 0' before '1 1' makes the same proof verify.
fix: kernel_propagate is the one home for publishing the root literals it forces, as Kissat writes every root-level assignment to the proof when it is made, so no caller can leave a kernel root unit implicit before a witnessed addition. propagate_service no longer duplicates the publication.
found_by: AM321 corpus replay of entry 015 under --random-policy=1 with the Satsuma+Kissat reference checking pipeline (backward dsr-trim, dsr-compress -d, Trestle).
name: unpublished-root-unit-before-witnessed-addition
oracle: Reference pipeline: dsr-trim VERIFIED but Trestle 's INVALID' on the elaborated LSR before the fix; both verify after it.
